say: Earth is basically a giant water planet. So why do people keep saying we could run out of drinking water?
Squash every ocean, lake and cloud into one ball, and it's only about eight hundred sixty miles wide. Kind of small, right?
Now the bad news. About ninety six and a half percent of all that water sits in the oceans, and it's way too salty to drink.
Only about two and a half percent is freshwater. If all of Earth's water fit in a one gallon jug, that's less than half a cup.
And most of that little cup is frozen solid. Almost seventy percent of the freshwater is locked up in ice caps and glaciers.
About thirty percent hides underground as groundwater. We pump some of it up with wells, but not all of it is easy to reach.
So what about every single lake and river on the planet? Added together, they're less than one hundredth of one percent of Earth's water.
Back in our gallon jug, that's just a few drops. And all the rivers in the world wouldn't even fill one single drop.
The good news? Water doesn't really disappear. The water cycle keeps recycling it, so the same water rains down on us again and again.
So maybe go easy on that tap. And follow Simply Weird for more weird stuff like this.
